$comment: Pinned PUC Lua builds for the MAINT-35 parse oracle, one per LuaLanguageLevel.
fetch-luac.py downloads each tarball, REFUSES on a sha256 mismatch, builds it and caches
test/luac/<version>/luac. ParseOracle resolves exactly that path and never consults PATH.
Why not a distro package: apt gives whatever the release carries (Debian ships 5.1.5-11,
5.4.8-x — patched, and floating with the distro). MAINT-33 pins every corpus checkout to a
commit SHA so the sweep is reproducible; pinning the corpus while letting the JUDGE drift is
incoherent. Worse, a PATH search lets two machines judge by different binaries while the gate
Checksums are lua.org's own published values (from the FTP index page — there are no .sha256
sidecars), each verified against the downloaded artefact on 2026-08-05. A self-computed digest
would only pin what we happened to download; it says nothing about authenticity.
Policy: pin the newest patch of each series. The grammar does not move within a patch series,
so an older patch is churn without benefit.
LUA50 is deliberately absent — PUC 5.0 is not a supported target, and requireBinary throws.
